Modern.brandNameRationale: Named for Iso E Super — the synthetic woody-amber molecule developed by IFF in 1973 — that defined minimalist molecule-forward perfumery, most famously in Escentric Molecules' Molecule 01 (2006). Iso E is a generic material name, not a trademark. The Atelier framing positions the brand as a single-perfumer house working with single materials.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern niche perfumery is crowded with story-led brands trading on travel and memory. There is room for a molecule-forward house that treats single materials as the entire composition — a perfumery that does for fragrance what single-origin coffee did for beans.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Escentric Molecules (escentric.com) holds the molecule-forward slot. Frédéric Malle (fredericmalle.com) is the perfumer-led peer. Le Labo (lelabofragrances.com) sets the modern-niche precedent. We sit closer to Escentric, sharper on single-material composition.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern niche perfumery built on single-material compositions.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 45. Owns five perfumes, not fifty. Reads Persolaise. Knows the difference between an absolute and a concrete.
behaviors: Reads the pyramid before the bottle copy

dos: Name the molecule on the bottle
Print the percentage in the formula
Speak in the language of olfactive material

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark. Iso E Atelier set in a tight modern grotesk, with the molecule formula (a small structural diagram) used as the hallmark beside the wordmark. The diagram alone is the favicon.

colorPalette.name: Iso Amber
colorPalette.meaning: Iso E Super's warm woody-amber character.

typography.primary: GT America for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for formulas and concentrations
typography.rationale: The mono carries the formula data. The regular carries the brand.

Luxury.tagline: The year the modern perfume began.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: Named for 1889 — the year Aimé Guerlain composed Jicky, often cited as the first modern perfume because it was the first to combine synthetic molecules (vanillin and coumarin) with naturals. The 1889 Hour references the watershed year without trading on any active mark (Guerlain remains an actively defended brand and is avoided). A luxury imprint anchored in the year the form was reinvented.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury perfumery is dominated by century-old houses (Guerlain, Caron, Houbigant, Lubin) and modern luxury collectors (Maison Francis Kurkdjian, Roja Parfums). The opportunity is a luxury imprint that takes a single year — the year the form was reinvented — as its entire editorial frame, releasing one fragrance annually that references a landmark composition of that era.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Roja Parfums (rojaparfums.com) holds the luxury-collector slot. Maison Francis Kurkdjian (franciskurkdjian.com) is the modern-luxury peer. By Kilian (bykilian.com) sets the luxury-niche precedent. We sit alongside Roja, sharper on the historical-anchor framing.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A luxury imprint releasing one fragrance a year, each anchored in the 1889 era of modern perfumery.

targetAudience.primary: 40 to 65. Owns vintage Guerlains. Reads Octavian Coifan. Buys 100ml bottles and keeps them in a cellar.
behaviors: Buys one annual release at full price
Reads the perfumer's notes before the marketing

dos: Name the year, the perfumer, the synthetic
Print the release year on the bottle
donts: Release more than one fragrance a year

Luxury.logoDirection: A serifed wordmark. The 1889 Hour set in a high-contrast classical serif, with the year 1889 set larger than the rest, used as the hallmark on every bottle. Foiled in gold on the cap.

typography.primary: Canela for the wordmark and bottle labels
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for batch numbers and release year
typography.rationale: Canela carries the imprint's archival stance. The mono carries the production data.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Named for sillage — the French perfumery term for the trail a fragrance leaves behind in a room or on a passerby. A one-word minimal brand whose entire promise is about how the scent moves through space. Sillage is a craft term, not a trademark.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal perfumery is well-served by Le Labo's typographic identity and a handful of one-word niche brands. There is still room for a one-word brand whose entire frame is sillage — the trail — rather than the bottle, the pyramid, or the story.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Le Labo (lelabofragrances.com) holds the typographic-minimal slot. Byredo (byredo.com) is the design-minimal peer. D.S. & Durga (dsanddurga.com) sets the niche-minimal precedent. We sit below all three on visual noise.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A minimal fragrance brand whose whole frame is the trail a scent leaves.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 45. Wears one fragrance a season. Decants for travel. Reads Now Smell This.
behaviors: Tests on skin, not on paper
Notes the sillage in a journal

dos: Describe the trail, not the top notes
Print the sillage rating on the label
Say nothing the bottle doesn't say

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark. SILLAGE set in a tight modern grotesk, with a single thin trailing line beneath the type that tapers off to the right, suggesting a scent trail. The trail alone is the favicon.

typography.secondary: Söhne Mono for sillage rating and concentration
typography.rationale: One typeface family. The mono carries the technical data, the regular carries the brand.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Named for the olfactive family classification system (floral, oriental, woody, chypre, fougère) used by the Société Française des Parfumeurs since 1984. As a corporate name, Olfactive Standard positions the house as catalog-organized — suits both retail and B2B private-label work. The olfactive-family taxonomy is industry-standard, not proprietary.
Corporate.industrySummary: Corporate fragrance houses (Givaudan, Firmenich, IFF, Symrise) supply the industry's compounding work but rarely brand themselves consumer-facing. There is room for a corporate-feeling fragrance house with a catalog organized strictly by olfactive family — readable to both retail buyers and B2B private-label clients.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Givaudan (givaudan.com) holds the B2B-compounding slot. Mane (mane.com) is the family-led B2B peer. Diptyque (diptyqueparis.com) sets the catalog-retail precedent. We sit between Diptyque and Mane.
Corporate.positioningStatement: A corporate fragrance house whose catalog is organized strictly by olfactive family.

targetAudience.primary: Retail buyers, hospitality fragrance buyers, private-label clients. Buys by olfactive family and concentration.

dos: Publish the olfactive family on every product

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a family-key hallmark. Olfactive Standard set in a clean grotesk, paired with a five-segment family-key icon (one segment per olfactive family). The key alone is the favicon.

typography.primary: Aktiv Grotesk for the wordmark and headers
typography.secondary: Aktiv Grotesk for body and catalog
typography.rationale: One typeface family. Reads professional on a sell sheet and clean on a catalog page.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Named for the historic oud trade — agarwood resin harvested in Southeast Asia and traded along the Arabian incense routes for over a thousand years. Oud Caravan positions the brand as a creative oud-forward niche imprint with a clear narrative of region, route, and material. Oud is a generic material name, not a trademark.
Creative.industrySummary: Oud-forward niche perfumery is a crowded but real segment — Amouage, Mancera, Ajmal, By Kilian's oud lines. There is creative room for an imprint that takes the trade route itself as its editorial frame, releasing fragrances tied to specific origin regions (Assam, Borneo, Cambodia, Laos).
Creative.competitorLandscape: Amouage (amouage.com) holds the heritage-oud slot. Mancera (mancera.com) is the contemporary-oud peer. Xerjoff (xerjoff.com) sets the luxury-oud precedent. We sit alongside Amouage, sharper on the route-and-origin framing.
Creative.positioningStatement: A creative oud-forward imprint organized by origin region and trade route.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 60. Loves oud. Owns three or four oud-forward bottles. Reads about agarwood grading.
behaviors: Reads the grade and the country

dos: Name the region, the harvest, the grade
Print the trade route on the back of every bottle

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark with a route line. Oud Caravan lettered in a contemporary serifed italic, with a small hand-drawn caravan-route line beneath that traces the historic incense route from Southeast Asia to Arabia. The route alone is the favicon.

typography.secondary: GT America Mono for region, grade, and harvest year
typography.rationale: The serif italic carries the imprint voice. The mono carries the origin data.
